creator: Unattributed (The New York World)
showsAccordingToSource: "Board game about journalist Nellie Bly's trip around the world in 1889-1890... flanked with images of Nellie Bly, Jules Verne, a steam ship, and a train. Illustration in 'The New York World', New York, N.Y., 26 January 1890, p. 21." (LoC ppmsca.02918, 'No known restrictions on publication')
storyLink: Document of the trip itself: Bly's promise/race against Verne's hero (Anchors: promise; y1.0) with Bly and Jules Verne drawn on the sheet, and a numbered square 'Go to Amiens' (the visit). Newspaper printed at the time of her trip.
pdReasonUS: Published 26 Jan 1890 in a US newspaper (pre-1931); LoC: no known restrictions.
pdReasonUKEU: Unattributed newspaper illustration, anonymous and 136 years old (>70).
captionDraft: The World's Round the World game, 1890
altDraft: A newspaper page with a spiral board game of numbered squares, a drawn woman in a checked dress at left and a bearded man labelled Jules Verne at right.
concerns: Busy, text-heavy page; at 640 px the squares are tiny, so it would need a crop (e.g. Bly and Verne corners). It is a souvenir game, not the Amiens visit. LoC page itself not fetched (loc.gov blocked); LoC id and statement taken from the Commons file page. Verne's portrait is a drawing by an unnamed artist.

creator: unknown
